claim: >-
  The descriptor and accepted defineModule helper are not competing runtime
  architectures: the descriptor remains inert domain data, while defineModule
  is an identity-preserving authoring facade. No reproducible P0-P2 defect was
  found. Two concrete documentation/API-state ambiguities remain.

    - "docs/requirements/module-system-v1.md:27-31 — declarations must remain inert."
    - "docs/requirements/module-system-v1.md:123-127 — public declarations must remain framework-independent."
    - "docs/decisions/0001-product-neutral-deterministic-module-composition.md:30-48 — Core owns inert composition, while products own executable and lifecycle authority."
    - "docs/decisions/0002-adopt-organization-feature-module-standard-v1.md:19-46 — feature ownership must avoid framework-owned composition and ceremonial layering."
    - "docs/decisions/0004-freeze-v1-portable-composition-contract-and-plan-digest.md:41-55 — ModuleDeclarationV1 is inert portable data."
    - "docs/decisions/0004-freeze-v1-portable-composition-contract-and-plan-digest.md:79-111 — the compiler, not an authoring helper, validates and produces the plan."
    - "docs/decisions/0006-clarify-v1-compiler-normalization-and-entry-points.md:155-172 — helpers are pure; exact generic signatures remain subject to packed-consumer evidence."
    - "docs/decisions/0007-require-executable-v1-conformance-amendments.md:427-450 — defineModule reads nothing, validates nothing, and returns the exact input reference."

observedBehavior:
  - "HEAD was detached at the exact requested SHA; git status and git diff were clean before and after review."
  - "The descriptor candidate directly authors an inert Declaration object at candidate-descriptor.ts:4-7."
  - "The defineModule candidate implements a one-line identity function at candidate-define.ts:3. A read-only Proxy probe reproduced reference identity with zero property reads."
  - "The runner requires all candidate decodings to preserve the same world digest at run.mjs:169-176 and requires one digest across candidates at run.mjs:228. Thus its semantic comparison does not establish a distinct runtime architecture for defineModule."
  - "The common runner was read and syntax-checked but not executed: it writes temporary files and tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/dist/result-summary.json at run.mjs:237-259,287-288, which would violate this assignment's read-only constraint."
applicability:
  scope: >-
    Limited to descriptor-object versus typed defineModule under
    Clean Architecture, SOLID, and DDD responsibility boundaries.
  exclusions:
    - "No cardinality-helper design decision."
    - "No dependency-record selection."
    - "No activation-factory selection."
    - "No public API authorization."
    - "No production-readiness or runtime-performance claim."
benefits:
  - "The descriptor remains portable, serializable domain data rather than an executable entity or service."
  - "An identity-only defineModule can improve literal inference without acquiring validation, registration, lifecycle, or DI responsibilities."
  - "Compiler-owned validation preserves single responsibility: authoring expresses intent; the compiler enforces the closed domain."
  - "Both forms preserve dependency inversion because no container, framework, loader, or product runtime type enters the declaration."
failureModes:
  - "Treating defineModule as a validating value-object constructor would contradict its accepted no-read/no-validation semantics."
  - "Adding factories, activation, registration, freezing, or normalization to defineModule would combine authoring, validation, and runtime responsibilities."
  - "Treating a value accepted by the TypeScript helper as already domain-valid would bypass compiler-owned invariants."
  - "Selecting a public helper signature from disposable fixtures would elevate qualification observations over accepted authority."
counterexamples:
  - "candidate-define.ts:3 proves defineModule can be erased to identity behavior; it does not encapsulate domain behavior."
  - "type-probes.ts:7 deliberately preserves an extra authorNote property, while corpus.ts:61 and run.mjs:184 require unknown declaration fields to be rejected by the compiler oracle."
  - "candidate-split.ts:3 owns ActivationFactory; candidate-define.ts contains no ActivationFactory."

findings:
  - severity: concrete-ambiguity
    location: "research/implementation-readiness/report.md:316"
    reproduction: >-
      git grep attributes a "typed activation seam" to typed defineModule, but
      ActivationFactory occurs only in candidate-split.ts:3, its re-export at
      common/index.ts:5, and the split import/use at type-probes.ts:2,21.
      candidate-define.ts:1-38 contains no activation seam. The exact-SHA
      read-only assertion returned
      {"reportAttributesActivationToDefineModule":true,"defineCandidateOwnsActivationFactory":false,"splitCandidateOwnsActivationFactory":true}.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Replace "typed activation seam" with "typed authoring/inference seam", or
      explicitly attribute activation to the separate product-owned/split
      boundary. Do not imply that activation belongs inside defineModule.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: false
  - severity: concrete-ambiguity
    location: >-
      docs/decisions/0006-clarify-v1-compiler-normalization-and-entry-points.md:169-172;
      docs/decisions/0009-keep-pre-1-0-public-api-unversioned.md:31-36;
      tests/qualification/implementation-readiness/api-authoring/common/type-probes.ts:5-7
    reproduction: >-
      The accepted authority defers the exact generic signature; proposed
      ADR-0009 lists ModuleDeclaration and defineModule without defining whether
      ModuleDeclaration denotes unchecked authoring data or a validated domain
      value. The fixture chooses T extends Declaration and proves an extra
      authorNote survives, while corpus.ts:61 and run.mjs:184 require the
      compiler to reject unknown declaration fields. The read-only assertion
      returned
      {"helperCandidatePreservesExtraField":true,"compilerOracleRejectsUnknownField":true}.
    minimalCorrection: >-
      Before accepting the public signature, state explicitly that defineModule
      returns unchecked authoring data and does not establish domain validity,
      or introduce a clearly distinguished validated type after compilation.
      Bind the choice with the already-required packed TypeScript,
      JavaScript/checkJs, and compiler-handoff tests.
    productOwnerDecisionRequired: true
openQuestions:
  - "Will the proposed public ModuleDeclaration type denote unchecked authoring syntax or a post-validation domain value?"
  - "Must the final generic signature reject excess properties statically, or is compiler-time unknown-field rejection the intentional boundary?"
confidence:
  level: high
  rationale: >-
    Both ambiguities have direct exact-SHA source proof and read-only
    reproductions. Confidence does not extend to runner pass status,
    packed-consumer inference, or production behavior because no production
    subject exists and the write-producing runner was not executed.
recommendedDecision: >-
  Preserve the accepted layering: inert descriptor data is the canonical
  composition language; defineModule may remain a zero-behavior typed authoring
  facade over that same data; validation belongs solely to the compiler and
  activation remains product-owned. Correct the activation attribution and
  close the unchecked-versus-validated type distinction through an accepted
  public-API decision and packed-consumer evidence. This report makes no public
  API selection.
conditionsToReverse:
  - "An accepted successor ADR changes defineModule runtime semantics with executable packed-subject evidence."
  - "Packed NodeNext, Bundler, JavaScript, and checkJs consumers show that an identity facade cannot provide the required inference without violating the inert boundary."
  - "Two production adapters demonstrate a necessary behavior that cannot be represented by the inert descriptor contract."
